components.name: OMD host runtime
components.limitations: Pinned Apple Silicon development host. The host is feature-agnostic and features are TypeScript mods; evidence is local and offline, and release qualification remains open.
components.removal: Select or reinstall the retained upstream executable; `OMD_MODE=upstream_direct` disables OMD task behaviour inside the custom binary.

components.name: Public TypeScript mod API
components.limitations: API 0.2 is experimental. API 0.1 admission and SDK declarations are retired in this development host; historical compatibility fixtures do not establish current support.
components.removal: Breaking stable changes need an API major with one stable OMD release of deprecation notice; each row has a finite support window in mods/COMPATIBILITY.md.

components.name: Mod package install, update and rollback
components.limitations: Local folders, Git repositories (a branch or tag locks to its commit), curated-index releases and npm packages from public or npmrc-configured private registries (sha512-verified, no runtime dependencies, npm install scripts never run). Installing never enables a mod, and granted permissions still run with that authority.
components.removal: `omd-mod` disable, uninstall, revoke and package-quarantine work without any control mod; disable and uninstall restore the previous lock and preserve edited sources and explicit settings, and quarantine blocks the installed version while keeping its data.

components.name: omd_coordination
components.limitations: API 0.2 service and command own delegation choices. The generic host enforces route, permission, snapshot and ledger boundaries; reviewed workflow parity remains under qualification.
components.removal: Disable the mod to remove its delegation policy; the generic host does not supply a hidden replacement policy.

components.name: omd_recovery
components.limitations: API 0.2 mod chooses bounded escalation and outage fallback from structured host results. Live provider quality and full resume parity remain open.
components.removal: Disable the mod to remove its recovery policy; generic host limits and contract restrictions remain.

components.name: omd_workspace
components.limitations: API 0.2 mod supplies terminal components. Native terminal parity and feature-code retirement remain open.
components.removal: Disable the mod to remove its layout; generic terminal controls remain.

components.name: Codex plugins (plugin.json)
components.limitations: Plugin discovery, MCP servers and hook execution stay upstream-owned and unmodified; OMD adds no plugin transport and does not sandbox plugin hooks.
components.removal: Remove the plugin from the Codex plugin directory; no OMD state refers to it.

components.name: Codex hooks
components.limitations: Hook dispatch is upstream-owned: competing pre_tool_use rewrites are still resolved by whichever hook finishes last. OMD's command-hook fixtures are synthetic and make no provider or full-session performance claim.
components.removal: Remove the hook file from the Codex configuration; mod interception is registered separately and is unaffected.

components.name: OMD guidance and hooks plugin
components.limitations: Explicitly installed and hash-trusted; skill selection is not a release default. PostToolUse records successful host results only. Its API 0.2 migration has local tests; live cadence and parity qualification remain open.
components.removal: Remove omd-guidance-hooks from Codex and the marketplace. Generic host contracts enforce only a document the user selected.

components.name: OMD review policy plugin
components.limitations: Explicitly installed and hash-trusted. Skills select prompts and cadence; hooks require a mod-owned review receipt when selected. Generic contracts enforce selected receipts and completion gates. Live review parity remains open.
components.removal: Remove omd-review-policy from Codex; unselected review prompts and hook cadence stop, while any user-selected generic contract remains enforced.

components.name: OMD application bridges plugin
components.limitations: Explicitly installed, hash-trusted and default-off. Adapter tools use generic host permissions and explicit service grants; full API 0.2 provider acceptance remains open.
components.removal: Remove omd-application-bridges from Codex and disable application_bridge. The managed browser bundle and dormant adapter sources remain until the private OMD installation is removed.

components.name: OMD artifact reading plugin
components.limitations: URL and GitHub reads use approved host web or shell tools; local PDF text and page images require installed Ghostscript. The helper bounds local files and outputs, never executes notebook cells, and cannot grant external content instruction authority. Optional current-API component registers github://; plugin-owned sandboxed helper supplies bounded reads. Real public source passed; private-account support remains unqualified.
components.removal: Remove omd-artifact-reading from Codex. Existing host web, shell and image tools remain available.

components.name: OMD code execution plugin

combinations.result: Both claimants of one `mod_<id>_<name>` slot and both claimants of one exclusive replacement point fail closed before activation; the remaining mod keeps its tool and command.

The first mod in composition order owns each key and later claims are reported as conflicts; bindings may target another mod's command, and a patch that claims a reserved native key is rejected by the host before the terminal sees it.

The bundled mods run with a contending terminal mod, a broken mod and a user/project duplicate: the contenders fail closed with source-located errors, coordination supplies bounded delegation preparation to recovery, and the remaining first-party behavior keeps working.

Disabling a provider refuses the transactional reload, and the next session disables only the required consumer; the optional consumer catches the absence, unrelated mods keep composing and the generated installed-contract types follow the active set.

An edited mod is swapped only at the next generation: the in-flight tool call keeps its source and forwards each progress update once, the stream middleware keeps its old transform until reload, stale generations are rejected and the replacement owner is unchanged.

Packages on the supported API row activate with per-package stability and feature negotiation; a package pinned to another host release or API is refused before activation, and a bumped state version keeps only that package inactive until its explicit migration runs.

The optional plugin exposes three separately selected skills and validates structured subagent output only when selected. The native reactive-guard marker projection was removed with the controlled host on 2026-09-27; the hooks run again in the default OMD session in Batch 2.55.
Explicit skills select review prompts; the selected hook requires a successful mod-owned review receipt. Generic contract gates still enforce their selected document independently.

Context observers run in activation order under the per-fragment limit; an observer that throws or exceeds its fragment is isolated and dropped for the runtime, and each package keeps a separate state file that a failing neighbour never creates or touches.
The managed bundle is injected into OMD alone, launches the exact bundled executable with its own profile, and a failed post-swap update restores the verified tree with no stray process.

The plugin exposes five prompt-approved adapter-scoped tools over one managed session. All adapters exchange events and exposed state; cross-adapter requests, unauthorized applications, oversized payloads and stale versions are refused, and teardown rotates the token, clears evidence and removes the connection file.

One TypeScript mod manages separate Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, Rust and Java server sessions over process.*. Semantic reads are scope-checked, edits are exact-scope and hash-bound with a host backup, an absent server is a visible non-success fallback, and a failed post-edit synchronisation restores the backup.

Both opt-in skill plugins are pinned in the same marketplace and install into an isolated Codex home without claiming a tool namespace. The artifact helper does not execute notebook cells; code execution uses the separate native host. Combined live task use remains untested.

Mod interceptors compose around a tool call: they rewrite, retarget, deny or answer it before the native handler, permission check and hook chain run, and inspect its result after; an answer is recorded as the mod's and cannot forge the native outcome, and upstream hook dispatch itself stays unmodified.

An approved sidecar and provider route start, serve and are torn down inside the owning task and generation; unapproved service IDs are refused, secrets stay opaque references and nothing survives task completion.

combinations.result: Two outside-author packages that replace coordination, context and the terminal run in one live session beside two repository-only conformance fixtures; the terminal's cross-mod keys reach both other packages, the context replacement drops evidence outside the declared scope before the worker sees it, and the same four packages install, upgrade from mod API `.5` to `.6` with a state migration, roll back and re-upgrade through the package manager.
The workflow and coordination mods compose through generic host services, checked integration and completion with local scripted providers; live provider qualification remains open.

regression.case: Composition, precedence and conflict handling on the current API 0.2 row: declared order, cycles, contested replacements and scope shadowing.
Package-owned state survives a host upgrade only through an explicit migration, with a content-addressed backup and an interrupted-migration rollback.
The shipped runtime patch still applies byte-for-byte to the pinned upstream commit and stays compatible with the recorded upstream surfaces.
Mods keep loading under the pinned Node erasable-TypeScript loader with no ambient process, fetch or code generation.
